title: Refrigerator not cooling but light is on
text: If the interior light works but the compartment is warm, first check the temperature dial or digital setpoint; a bumped dial is the most common cause. Next confirm the condenser coils behind or beneath the unit are not caked with dust, since blocked coils cannot shed heat. Listen for the compressor: a hum with no cooling points to a failed start relay, while silence points to the control board or thermostat. Allow 24 hours after any change before judging the result.

title: Ice maker stopped producing ice
text: Confirm the ice maker arm or paddle is in the down (on) position and the freezer is at or below 0 F (-18 C). Inspect the water supply line for kinks and verify the inlet valve opens when the cycle starts; a valve that hums but passes no water is usually clogged by sediment. If the mold heater has failed the tray will fill but never eject. Replace the water filter if it is more than six months old, because a saturated filter starves the fill cycle.

title: Water dispenser flow is slow or stopped
text: Slow dispenser flow is almost always the water filter: replace it and flush two gallons. If flow is still weak, check the household shutoff valve and the inlet valve screen for scale. In freezers with a dispenser line routed through the door, a frozen section of tubing will block flow entirely; leave the door open for thirty minutes to thaw, then look for the cause of the freeze such as a torn door gasket.

title: Error code E-FF on refrigerator display
text: Code E-FF indicates the freezer fan motor is not reporting rotation. Unplug the unit, remove the evaporator cover, and check for ice build-up around the fan blade; a frost-locked fan is common after a defrost heater failure. If the blade spins freely, measure the fan motor windings and the harness connector. Clear the code by power-cycling the unit after the repair.

title: Front-load washer will not drain
text: When a front-load washer stops with standing water, open the small access panel at the lower front and clean the drain pump filter; coins, hair ties and lint are the usual culprits. Check that the drain hose is not inserted more than eight inches into the standpipe, which creates a siphon lock. If the pump runs but does not move water, the impeller may be broken. A pump that is silent needs its winding resistance checked.

title: Washer error code OE
text: OE is the drain error. The washer tried to drain for ten minutes and the water level sensor still detected water. Follow KB-005: clean the pump filter, check the drain hose height (between 30 and 96 inches), and confirm the standpipe is not clogged. If the pressure switch hose has fallen off the tub, the sensor will never see an empty tub and OE will repeat.

title: Washer shakes violently during spin
text: Excessive vibration during spin usually means the shipping bolts were never removed from the back of the machine, or the unit is not level. Remove all four transit bolts and adjust the leveling feet until the cabinet does not rock diagonally. Small loads of a single heavy item, such as one bath mat, will also unbalance the drum; add towels to balance. If the noise is a rhythmic knocking, the suspension rods or shock absorbers may be worn.

title: Washer error code UE unbalanced load
text: UE means the drum could not balance the load before spin. Redistribute the laundry, avoid washing one heavy item alone, and confirm the machine is level on all four feet. If UE appears with every load including an empty drum, the hall sensor on the motor or the shock absorbers should be inspected.

title: Dryer runs but produces no heat
text: A dryer that tumbles without heat usually has a blown thermal fuse, which fails open when exhaust airflow is restricted. Before replacing the fuse, clean the lint screen, the lint chute, and the full length of the exhaust duct, otherwise the new fuse will fail again. On electric dryers also confirm both legs of the 240 V supply are present; a tripped half of a double-pole breaker lets the motor run while the heating element stays cold. On gas dryers check the igniter glow and the gas valve coils.

title: Dryer takes two or more cycles to dry
text: Long dry times are an airflow problem until proven otherwise. Measure the exhaust: a duct longer than 25 feet, or with more than two elbows, needs a booster or rerouting. Foil or plastic flexible duct sags and traps lint and should be replaced with rigid metal. A clogged outside vent flap is a frequent hidden cause. Only after airflow is verified should the moisture sensor bars be cleaned with rubbing alcohol.

title: Dryer error code d80 d90 d95
text: The d80, d90 and d95 codes report restricted exhaust airflow at 80, 90 and 95 percent blockage respectively. This is a flow sensor reading, not a component failure. Disconnect the duct at the dryer and run a timed cycle: if the code clears, the blockage is in the duct or the wall vent. Clean the entire duct run and the exterior hood.

title: Dishwasher leaves dishes wet
text: Poor drying is expected with plastic items, which do not hold heat. For glass and ceramic, confirm rinse aid is filled, because the rinse aid dispenser is what makes water sheet off. Check that the heating element is energized at the end of the wash and that the vent fan runs. Opening the door a few inches at the end of the cycle greatly improves drying on models without a fan.

title: Dishwasher not filling with water
text: If the dishwasher hums but stays dry, verify the water supply valve under the sink is open and the inlet valve screen is clear. A float switch stuck in the up position by debris will block the fill. The door must latch fully; a worn latch prevents the fill circuit from closing. Measure voltage at the inlet valve during the fill phase to separate a bad valve from a control problem.

title: Dishwasher error code AE or E1 leak detected
text: AE (or E1 on some models) means water reached the leak sensor in the base pan. Common causes are a sump gasket leak, a loose drain hose clamp, or over-sudsing from hand dish soap. Tip the unit slightly and dry the base pan completely before restarting, or the code will return immediately. Inspect the door gasket for cuts along the bottom edge.

title: Oven temperature runs hot or cold
text: If baked goods burn on the bottom or take too long, verify the oven with a standalone thermometer at 350 F for twenty minutes; a variance under 25 degrees is normal. Larger differences are corrected with the oven calibration offset in the settings menu, typically adjustable plus or minus 35 degrees. A temperature that swings widely points to a failing temperature sensor probe, which should read about 1,080 ohms at room temperature.

title: Oven error code F9 or F-9 door lock
text: F9 indicates the door lock motor did not reach the locked or unlocked position within the time limit. This usually appears after a self-clean cycle. Let the oven cool fully, then power-cycle at the breaker. If the code returns, inspect the lock motor cam and the switch that reports its position. Do not force the door open while the latch is engaged.

title: Gas cooktop burner will not light
text: A burner that clicks but does not light has a gas or alignment problem; one that does not click has an ignition problem. Confirm the burner cap is seated correctly and the ports are clear of food debris. Dry the igniter after spills. If all burners click continuously even when off, moisture in the spark module or a shorted igniter wire is the cause.

title: Induction cooktop shows U or does not heat
text: A U symbol or a flashing zone indicator means the cooktop does not detect suitable cookware. Only ferromagnetic pans work; test with a magnet on the pan base. The pan must also cover most of the zone. Pans with warped bases may be detected intermittently and cause the zone to cycle on and off.

title: Microwave runs but does not heat food
text: A microwave that lights, turns the plate, and hums but does not heat almost always has a failed magnetron, high-voltage diode, or high-voltage capacitor. These parts hold a lethal charge even when unplugged; only trained technicians should open the cabinet. The door interlock switches can also cause a no-heat condition when one switch fails while the others still let the unit run.

title: Microwave sparking or arcing inside
text: Arcing inside the cavity is usually caused by a damaged waveguide cover, metal trim on dishes, or a chipped rack support. Replace the mica waveguide cover if it is burnt or greasy. Inspect the cavity paint for chips exposing bare metal and touch up with microwave-safe cavity paint.

title: Range hood fan is loud or weak
text: A loud hood is usually a loose blower wheel or a fan motor with worn bearings. Weak airflow points to grease-clogged filters, a duct run with too many bends, or a damper flap stuck closed at the roof or wall cap. Clean aluminum mesh filters in the dishwasher monthly; replace charcoal filters every six months on recirculating models.

title: Air conditioner blowing warm air
text: A window or portable AC that runs but blows warm air should first have its filter cleaned and the mode confirmed as Cool rather than Fan. On split systems check that the outdoor unit is running; a stopped condenser fan or a tripped outdoor disconnect leaves the indoor unit circulating room-temperature air. Frost on the evaporator coil indicates low refrigerant or restricted airflow and requires a technician.

title: Air conditioner error code CH05 or CH 05
text: CH05 on a split system means the indoor and outdoor units have lost communication. Check the four-core interconnect cable for correct terminal order at both ends, especially after installation. Reset power at the breaker for five minutes. A damaged communication wire in the wall or a failed outdoor PCB are the next suspects.

title: Portable air conditioner keeps shutting off
text: A portable AC that stops after a short time is usually full of condensate; empty the internal tank or install the continuous drain hose. Check the filter and confirm the exhaust hose is as short and straight as possible, since a long kinked hose overheats the unit and trips the thermal protector.

title: Dehumidifier not collecting water
text: If the dehumidifier fan runs but the bucket stays empty, the room may already be below the humidity setpoint, so lower the setting first. Room temperature below 65 F causes the coil to frost and most units will stop the compressor until it thaws. Clean the filter and check that the bucket is seated so the float switch is released.

title: TV has sound but no picture
text: Sound without picture points to the backlight or the LED driver. In a dark room shine a flashlight at the screen; if a faint image is visible the panel works and the backlight has failed. If nothing is visible even with the flashlight, the main board or T-con board is suspect. A screen that flashes on and then goes black within seconds is the classic symptom of a failing LED strip.

title: TV remote not responding
text: Replace the batteries first, then check the infrared emitter by looking at the remote through a phone camera while pressing a button; the emitter should flash. On Bluetooth or magic remotes re-pair by holding the OK or wheel button for five seconds near the TV. Fluorescent or LED lighting close to the TV can swamp the IR receiver.

title: TV will not connect to Wi-Fi
text: When the TV finds the network but cannot connect, confirm the router is not set to 5 GHz only on older sets and that the password has no unsupported characters. Set the TV DNS to 8.8.8.8 manually if the connection succeeds but apps fail to load. A TV placed inside a metal cabinet may have too weak a signal; a wired Ethernet cable resolves most persistent cases.

title: TV screen has vertical lines
text: Persistent vertical lines that appear in every input, including the TV menu, are a panel or T-con board fault, not a source problem. Lines that appear only on one HDMI input point to the cable or the source device. Gently press on the bezel edge near the lines; if they change, the flexible panel ribbon connection has loosened and the panel usually needs replacement.

title: Soundbar not producing sound over HDMI ARC
text: For ARC to work the HDMI cable must be in the ARC-labeled port on both the TV and soundbar, HDMI-CEC (often branded SimpLink or Anynet+) must be enabled on both, and the TV audio output must be set to external speaker or HDMI ARC. Power-cycle both devices after changing settings. Some older cables lack the ARC channel; use a High Speed HDMI cable.

title: Robot vacuum keeps stopping and reporting an obstacle
text: Repeated obstacle stops usually mean the bumper sensor is stuck or the cliff sensors are dirty. Wipe all sensors with a dry cloth and confirm the bumper clicks freely on both sides. Dark rugs can trigger cliff sensors; use the no-go zone feature in the app. Hair wrapped around the main brush or side wheels also causes false obstacle reports.

title: Robot vacuum battery drains quickly
text: Battery run time drops when the brush roll is clogged, which raises motor current. Clean the brush, the bin filter, and the wheel axles. Batteries older than two to three years lose capacity and should be replaced with the correct part number. Always dock the unit after use; storing it discharged shortens battery life.

title: Water heater pilot light will not stay lit
text: A pilot that lights but goes out when the knob is released indicates a weak or dirty thermocouple. Clean the tip with fine sandpaper and make sure it is fully in the pilot flame. If the flame is yellow and lazy, the pilot orifice is partially blocked. Replace the thermocouple if cleaning does not help; it is an inexpensive part.

title: How to reset the water filter indicator
text: After installing a new refrigerator filter, hold the Filter or Water Filter button on the dispenser panel for three seconds until the indicator returns to green or the light goes out. On models with a touchscreen, use Settings then Filter Reset. The indicator is a timer, typically six months, and does not measure actual filter condition.

title: How to enter service or diagnostic mode on a refrigerator
text: On most refrigerators, press and hold the Refrigerator and Ice Plus buttons together for about five seconds until the display beeps, then use the Freezer button to step through test modes. Test modes run the compressor, fans, and defrost heater independently so each can be verified in a few minutes. Exit by pressing the same combination or by cycling power.

title: Using the SmartThinQ or ThinQ app to read error history
text: Connect the appliance to the app, open the device, and choose Smart Diagnosis. The app records recent error codes with timestamps, which is faster than asking the customer to recall the sequence. For appliances without Wi-Fi, hold the phone microphone to the speaker on the control panel and press and hold the Smart Diagnosis button; the tone sequence encodes the same data.

title: Warranty coverage for compressors and sealed system
text: The linear compressor carries a ten-year limited parts warranty; labor is covered for the first year unless an extended plan applies. Sealed system repairs, which include the compressor, condenser, evaporator and refrigerant lines, must be performed by an authorized technician for the warranty to remain valid. Cosmetic parts and consumables such as water filters and light bulbs are not covered.

title: Escalation path for repeat repair visits
text: If a unit requires a third visit for the same symptom within ninety days, open a Repeat Repair escalation in the service portal before dispatching. The escalation attaches the previous work orders and triggers a review for unit replacement. Document the symptom, the parts already replaced, and the customer's preferred contact window.

title: Service ticket priority levels
text: Priority 1 covers safety issues such as gas smell, sparking, or water leaking near electrical parts, and must be dispatched the same day. Priority 2 is a total loss of function on a refrigerator or freezer, dispatched within 48 hours. Priority 3 covers partial function loss and Priority 4 covers cosmetic or noise complaints, scheduled at the next available slot.

title: Required photos before parts are ordered
text: To avoid returned parts, every order must include a photo of the model and serial label, a photo of the failed component in place, and, for boards, a photo of the connector side. Blurry label photos are the top cause of wrong-part shipments. Upload photos to the work order before submitting the parts request.

title: Refrigerator door not sealing properly
text: Test the gasket by closing the door on a strip of paper; if the paper slides out with no resistance the seal is weak at that point. Clean the gasket with warm soapy water, then apply a thin film of petroleum jelly to restore flexibility. Check that the refrigerator is tilted slightly backward so the doors swing closed on their own. A gasket that is torn or has lost its magnet must be replaced.

title: Freezer frost build-up on the back wall
text: Heavy frost on the back wall of a frost-free freezer means the automatic defrost system has failed. The three components are the defrost heater, the defrost thermostat (bi-metal), and the defrost timer or control board. Enter diagnostic mode (KB-035) and force a defrost cycle; if the heater does not warm within a few minutes, test the heater and thermostat for continuity.

title: Washer leaving clothes soaking wet
text: If clothes are wet at the end of the cycle but the machine drained, the final spin was skipped or shortened, usually because of an unbalanced load (KB-008) or a selected low-spin or delicate cycle. If the drum never reached high speed, check the motor hall sensor and the drive belt on belt-driven models. Clogged drain pumps also cause this because the machine will not spin with water still in the tub.

title: Washer door will not unlock after cycle
text: The door lock stays engaged until the water level sensor reports the tub empty and the drum has stopped. Wait two minutes after the cycle ends. If it still will not open, the tub probably has water in it; run a drain-and-spin cycle or drain manually through the pump filter hose. A lock that never releases even when dry indicates a failed door lock assembly.

title: Dryer drum not turning
text: If the motor hums but the drum does not turn, the drive belt is broken or slipped off the idler pulley. If nothing happens at all, check the door switch, the thermal fuse, and the start switch. A drum that turns by hand with a squeal points to worn drum rollers or the idler pulley bearing.

title: Dishwasher not cleaning well on top rack
text: Weak top-rack washing usually means the upper spray arm is not receiving water. Check that the arm spins freely and its holes are not clogged with food or mineral deposits; soak the arm in vinegar. Confirm the water supply tube to the upper arm is connected when the rack is pushed in. Overloading the lower rack with tall items blocks water from reaching the upper arm.

title: Oven light or convection fan not working
text: A convection fan that does not run while the bake element works is typically a failed fan motor or a control relay. The fan only runs in convection modes, so confirm the mode first. An oven light that does not come on with the door switch is usually just the bulb, but check the socket for heat damage.

title: Handling a customer report of a gas smell
text: Treat any report of a gas smell as Priority 1 (KB-039). Instruct the customer to leave the home, avoid switching lights or appliances, and call the gas utility from outside. Do not schedule a technician until the utility has cleared the home. Document the call time and the instructions given in the ticket.
